# Osteoma Cutis

**Authors:** Faten Limaiem, Shane R. Sergent

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Osteoma cutis or cutaneous ossification is a rare and benign dermatological disease characterized by bone formation in the dermis or subcutaneous tissue. It can be either primary when it occurs de novo without a pre-existing disease or secondary when it develops in association with an underlying condition such as trauma, neoplastic or inflammatory diseases. Osteoma cutis can affect children as well as adults. Primary osteoma cutis accounts for 15% of the patients, whereas secondary osteoma cutis represents 85% of the cases. The histogenesis of this dermatological condition has not been fully established.
